title: Être: understand, practice and remember
introduction: Development-only fixture, not independently reviewed for publication. Use être (to be) to say who someone is or where they are. Read the examples, then try six short activities.
explanation: Être changes with the subject. Use suis with je (I), es with tu (you, informal singular), and est with il or elle (he or she). In Je suis étudiant, étudiant is masculine; étudiante is feminine. Both describe a student.
when_to_use: Use these forms to introduce yourself or say where someone is. Ici means here. Tu addresses one person informally.
recap: Je suis, tu es, il est, elle est. Choose the form that agrees with the subject.

exercises.explanation: With je, être becomes suis: je suis.

exercises.explanation: With tu, use es: tu es ici means you are here.

exercises.explanation: Je means I, tu means you, and elle means she. Ici means here.

exercises.instructions: Write one short sentence. Use French accents.
